title: Deeper/broader parser-assurance methods and validation cost
mode: Primary-source review of open-source DWG/DXF test, fuzz, diagnostic, and recovery methods
scope: Compare route separation in LibreDWG's corpus and fuzz workflows
Review peer diagnostics and sample-corpus evidence boundaries
Refine fast per-slice and composed-checkpoint validation sequencing

method.kind: Read current primary repository documentation and build/test metadata; no peer execution

sources.observed: Documents AFL, honggfuzz, and LLVM libFuzzer approaches, sanitizer configurations, and seeded corpus use. The guidance is methodology, not evidence of current libdxfrw defects or semantic correctness.
Defines separate DWG-read, DXF, Binary-DXF, JSON, SVG, and OSS-Fuzz corpus checks. This supports route separation, not importing its corpus, limits, or CI cadence.

The workflow includes platform-specific build and test jobs and configuration-specific coverage steps. It does not establish that the documented fuzz workflows run on every change; no claim about its runtime or cadence is transferred.
Reader examples expose an OnNotification event for warnings and information, so a peer comparison can capture diagnostics beyond a success/failure result.
The maintainer says the samples directory contains files used by the Tests project. This does not establish independent authoring or a normative expected result for every sample.
Strict reading is distinguished from slower ASCII-only recovery; recovery repairs structural flaws, runs audit, and warns that some decode/rewrite paths may lose information or yield invalid DXF.

sources.project: ezdxf audit launcher and feature documentation
sources.observed: The CLI exposes a separate audit/recovery operation; the feature summary documents direct ASCII and Binary DXF read/write. A peer audit is the peer's own model and does not replace independent expected-value checks.

planUpdates: Keep strict valid-input parsing separate from malformed ASCII recovery and repair/audit outcomes.
Capture peer notifications and source-to-output disposition rather than treating no exception as semantic success.
Retain focused generated checks and one owning CTest per slice; reserve bounded corpus, fuzz, and sanitizer work for composed security checkpoints.
Restrict fuzzer seeds and minimized reproducers to existing allowed fixtures or scratch-generated local data.
assessment.limitations: Sources are mutable project docs and implementation guidance; no peer, fuzzer, sanitizer, CAD application, or external file was run. No defect or support claim follows from this review.
